Large cohort studies and several systematic reviews have explored the relationship between the consumption of ﬁber, including
the source of ﬁber, and the risk of developing IBD. The Nurses’ Health Study prospectively followed up 170,776 women for 26 years
and demonstrated that women with an intake of fruit-derived ﬁber in the highest quartile (median 24.3 g/day) was associated with
a 40% reduction in risk of CD (multivariate HR 0.59, CI 0.39–0.90) compared with women in the lowest quartile of ﬁber consump-
tion (median 11.6 g/day). This apparent risk reduction appeared greatest for ﬁber derived from fruits,
